name: Non-androgenic cycle compounds (19-nor)

card.summary: A forum approach of using nandrolone-type (19-nor) anabolic agents, which are weakly androgenic in skin and scalp, to build muscle while aiming to limit androgen effects such as hair loss and acne.
card.note: Controlled substances in many countries; documented risks include suppression of natural hormone production and cardiovascular and fertility effects.

quick.overview:
The '19-nor' approach refers to anabolic steroids derived from nandrolone (19-nortestosterone), a testosterone analogue lacking one carbon group. Forum users who care about their hairline and skin discuss it because nandrolone is converted in the scalp and skin into a much weaker androgen than testosterone's potent DHT, which they take to mean fewer androgenic effects on hair and skin.

The appearance goal is a more muscular physique while trying to protect hair and skin. Medical references describe nandrolone as having strong anabolic and weak androgenic effects, but also as strongly progestogenic and suppressive of the body's own hormone signaling, so the approach has its own documented side effects.
quick.how: Descriptions in communities center on the idea of choosing 19-nor compounds over testosterone-derived ones for people worried about androgenic side effects. Specific compounds, amounts and schedules are not covered here. These agents are prescription or controlled substances, and non-medical use is generally illicit.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports nandrolone is a controlled substance in many countries (Schedule III in the US, Class C in the UK). Reported effects include suppression of natural gonadotropins, hypogonadism and infertility at high exposure, cardiovascular toxicity, acne and hair growth in women, and a possible, described-as-theoretical, risk to scalp hair. Nandrolone has been banned in Olympic sport since 1974.

lead: Non-androgenic cycle compounds, or '19-nor' compounds, are anabolic steroids related to nandrolone (19-nortestosterone), the C19-demethylated analogue of testosterone and the parent of a number of other anabolic steroids and progestins [1]. They come up in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums as an alternative for people who want muscle but are anxious about androgen-driven hair loss, acne and similar effects.

The reasoning draws on a real pharmacological difference. Testosterone is converted to the more potent dihydrotestosterone (DHT) in androgen-sensitive tissue such as the scalp, whereas nandrolone is not potentiated this way; the enzyme 5-alpha-reductase converts it to 5-alpha-dihydronandrolone, a much weaker ligand of the androgen receptor, which lessens effects in skin, scalp and prostate [1]. Wikipedia nonetheless notes that nandrolone may still cause scalp hair loss, which it describes as theoretical [1].

Nandrolone was first synthesized in 1950 and introduced medically as the phenylpropionate ester in 1959 and the decanoate ester in 1962; medical uses have included anemia, cachexia, osteoporosis and breast cancer, and use is now increasingly rare [1]. It is also a potent progestogen with antigonadotropic effects, and is controlled in many jurisdictions [1].

angle.goal: Muscle with hair and skin protection
chain: Strong anabolic effect, weak androgenic activity in scalp and skin
More muscle with less DHT-type hair and skin effect, as proponents hope
angle.text: People use the 19-nor idea to chase a bigger physique while trying to limit androgen effects on hairline and skin. The hair-sparing claim is based on nandrolone's weak conversion product, and sources describe hair loss from it as theoretical rather than ruled out.

infobox: Controlled in many countries (US Schedule III, UK Class C)

paras: The 19-nor group consists of steroids that lack the carbon-19 methyl group present in testosterone. Nandrolone is the parent compound and has a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio, with strong anabolic and weak androgenic effects [1]. Related prohormones in the 19-nor family, such as 19-nor-androstenedione and 19-nor-androstenediol, were sold as supplements in the past [2].

Unlike testosterone, nandrolone is not boosted into a stronger androgen in tissues containing 5-alpha-reductase. Instead the enzyme converts it to a weaker ligand, 5-alpha-dihydronandrolone, which reduces effects in the skin, scalp and prostate [1]. Nandrolone also binds the progesterone receptor at about 22 percent of progesterone's affinity, which contributes to suppression of gonadotropins [1].

In women, reported effects include acne, facial and body hair growth, voice deepening and clitoral enlargement, generally milder than with testosterone [1]. At high exposure, cardiovascular toxicity, hypogonadism and infertility may occur, and gynecomastia and reduced libido are possible [1]. Androgenic effects remain significant with prolonged use, including hirsutism and voice deepening in women and children [1].

Nandrolone has been prohibited in Olympic sport since 1974, with a urinary 19-norandrosterone threshold of 2.0 micrograms per litre; Wikipedia notes past detection problems and positive tests traced to contaminated androstenedione supplements [1]. Following the 2004 Anabolic Steroid Control Act, androstenedione and related steroids became controlled in the US, and as of January 2005 could not be sold without prescription [2].

A review of testosterone prohormone supplements, including 19-nor-androstenedione and 19-nor-androstenediol, found that prohormone supplements did not produce anabolic or ergogenic effects in men and might raise the risk of negative health consequences [2]. A randomized trial also examined norandrostenedione and norandrostenediol in resistance-trained men [3]. No trials have tested a '19-nor' approach for protecting hair or skin.

timeline.event: Androstenedione and related steroids no longer sold without prescription in the US [2].

lore.intro: In bodybuilding and hair-conscious communities, 19-nor agents are discussed as an option for people who want to limit androgenic effects, though the assumption that they spare hair is not firmly established.

claims.claim: 19-nor compounds are gentler on hair and skin than testosterone-based ones
claims.believers: Proponents note that nandrolone is converted to a weaker androgen in scalp and skin rather than DHT, so they expect fewer androgenic effects.
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes the weaker conversion product but says scalp hair loss from nandrolone may still occur, calling it theoretical [1].

claims.believers: Such products were marketed as muscle-building supplements.
claims.experts: A review concluded prohormone supplements, including 19-nor forms, did not produce anabolic or ergogenic effects in men and may raise health risks [2].
